waves.name: The one batch chain: MAINJOB, PGMMAIN, PGMLIVE
waves.rationale: The tree has one entry point, job:MAINJOB. It runs PGMMAIN, which calls PGMLIVE. The three touch no dataset, and there are no computed calls, so the seed puts them in one family and nothing forces a cut. Splitting the chain would leave a job with no program or a program with no caller. The wave passes the deploy, rollback and boundary tests only weakly: it can be flagged on and off as one job, but its only observable output is a return code, because the job has no DD statements. It passes the fourth test only if the client confirms job:MAINJOB is the nightly batch cycle. Nothing in the tree says so.
waves.unblocks: Nothing inside the tree. No live unit outside the wave depends on it. It proves the toolchain and the job-level comparison harness, which is a chore unless the client confirms it is the nightly batch cycle.

unassigned.reason: No static path from any entry point and no computed call in the tree. It joins no wave. Proposed for deletion, provisional until telemetry or the full JCL library confirms it (05-dead-code.md).
